notes: The title is COMMENTS ON "PURSUING STACKS", underlined throughout. The eleven correction entries comprise seven before Section 14 etc and four after it.

The p3 comment calls the comparison between cubical and simplicial sets interesting. It lists three numbered points: cartesian closure, the stated homotopy-category equivalence through realisation, and realisation of products with the stated fine-topology qualification.

Item 3 continues with the place of simplicial sets in the literature, a Dold-Kan equivalence stated for chain complexes without an explicit degree qualifier, and a published simplicial proof of the Serre spectral sequence attributed to A. Dress, referring to the author's paper with Heath, "Cogluing homotopy equivalences".
The final paragraph mentions Massey and Brown-Higgins as users of cubical methods and stops after not firmly embedded in the; the unfinished ending is preserved.
The lower-left 12 is archive numbering, retained only as a comment. The sheet has no typed page number, date, signature or total page count.

math_checks.outcome: Checked the possible degree-range ambiguity in the unqualified phrase chain complexes. For normalization of a simplicial abelian group, degrees below 0 are zero because the simplicial indexing begins at 0. A chain complex with Z in degree -1 and zero elsewhere therefore cannot be isomorphic to such a normalized complex. Thus the stated equivalence needs a nonnegative convention if chain complexes might otherwise mean all integer-graded complexes. The conventional nonnegative interpretation remains possible, so this is a qualification check, not a refutation of the author's intended statement. No qualifier absent from the ink is supplied in reading.tex.
